1.why: The reset token hash is stored in and validated against the requester's own session (`active.resetTokenHash` compared with `safeEqual`), so a code only works for the session/user it was issued to.

2.why: Reset tokens are bound to the issuing session's state, so a code presented from a different session has no matching `resetTokenHash` and is rejected — the statement is false of this system.

3.why: There is no invalidation of other/previous sessions on password change — the resetting session itself continues (only `verifiedResetAuthorization` is cleared), and no global session-revocation logic exists, so pre-reset sessions would remain valid.

4.why: `Bun.serve` is configured TLS-only with cert/key, HSTS and `upgrade-insecure-requests` are set, and non-HTTPS `x-forwarded-proto` is rejected; TLS version is not pinned but Bun negotiates modern TLS 1.3 by default.

5.why: Reset tokens and the MFA code are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and the password uses `Bun.password.hash` with bcrypt (cost 10), all generated from `crypto.getRandomValues`.

6.why: No email is ever composed or sent; the 'simulated delivery' returns the raw recovery token and MFA code in the JSON response and prints them into the page log/console, so there is no email-side protection of private data.

7.why: All inputs pass strict allowlist regexes (`validAccountInput`, `validToken`, `validPassword`, `/^\d{6}$/`), JSON bodies are size/type checked, and no user data is ever interpolated into HTML — client output uses `textContent`.

8.why: The only generated link is the relative internal path `/reset?stage=verify&token=...` with the token URL-encoded; no user-controlled outgoing URLs or redirects exist.

9.why: There are no email templates at all in this application, so the claim cannot be verified as true; the analogous simulated delivery output is at least script-safe via `textContent`.

10.why: The recovery token and the MFA security code are deliberately written to the visible 'Secure activity log' and browser console (`log("SIMULATED RESET DELIVERY — recovery token: " ...)`, `mockCode`), so tokens are exposed in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but the security code is hardcoded in source as `const MFA_CODE = "482915"`, so secret codes are stored in the code.

12.why: The fixed, hardcoded `MFA_CODE = "482915"` functions as a default/static credential for the second factor for every session, even though the password policy itself is strong.

13.why: Both `/api/verify-token` and `/api/mfa` count failures and impose a 60-second block after 5 wrong attempts (`resetBlockedUntil`, `mfaBlockedUntil`) returning HTTP 429.

14.why: `/api/recovery` always returns the same neutral message ('If the entered account information is eligible...') regardless of input, and there is no account lookup that could leak existence.

15.why: Tokens come from `randomValue(32)` using `crypto.getRandomValues` (32 bytes, base64url), are hashed, single-use, 10-minute-lived, and bound to the requesting session.
